conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Patel. I understand you've been having abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting again. Can you tell me more about what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it started a few days ago. I just got back from vacation and I think I overdid it. The pain is right here in the middle, above my belly button. It feels like the last time I had that ulcer issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And have you been able to keep your tube feeds going?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been trying, but I’ve been so nauseous. I’ve slowed them down a bit. I haven’t vomited through the tube, but I feel really full and uncomfortable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense. Given your history with the GJ ulcer and recent symptoms, we’re going to keep you NPO—nothing by mouth—for now and give you IV fluids to stay hydrated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So no tube feeds at all?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll pause the tube feeds for tonight. We want to let your stomach rest. We’ll continue your medications through the G-tube as needed, but the nutrition will come through the IV for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that’s fine. I just don’t want another ulcer.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re giving you an IV proton-pump inhibitor—lansoprazole—to help protect your stomach lining, just like before. And we’ll monitor your symptoms closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve been on that at home. Is it the same dose?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, same dose—30 mg twice a day, but now it’s IV so it works faster. We also gave you some ondansetron for nausea and morphine for pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: The morphine helped a little, but I didn’t want too much. I get sleepy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s okay—we’ll use it only as needed. Your labs came back normal—white count is fine, liver enzymes are okay, lipase is normal—so no signs of infection or pancreatitis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. I was worried about my liver too, since I’ve had fatty liver in the past.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your ALT and AST are normal, and bilirubin is fine. Alkaline phosphatase is a bit high, but not concerning. We’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better, actually. The pain is less intense. I haven’t needed any pain meds since last night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. We’re going to restart your tube feeds today, but at a slower rate—50 cc/hr instead of 60. We’ll see how you tolerate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Should I adjust anything at home after this?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep you on the same meds—rifaximin for bacterial overgrowth, lansoprazole, and your antidepressants. No changes there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the iron? My ferritin was low last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your ferritin is still low at 13, so we’re keeping you on ferrous sulfate. We’ll check it again at your follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, good. I’ve been taking it with vitamin C to help absorption.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s smart. You’re doing everything right. Let’s focus on getting your feeds back up slowly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. How’s the feeding going?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So far so good. No nausea, no pain. I’m actually feeling stronger.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Excellent. We’ll keep the feeds at 50 cc/hr for now. Your physical exam is normal—soft belly, no tenderness. That’s a good sign.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Do we know if it was another ulcer or just irritation?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We don’t have an endoscopy this time, but given your response to the PPI and symptom improvement, it’s likely irritation or early ulcer healing. We’ll follow up with GI soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll make sure to keep that appointment.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi again. Your team just documented the nutrition adjustment—feeds are continuing at 50 cc/hr. You’re doing well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. I feel like I’m back to my baseline. Can I go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly tomorrow. We want to make sure you stay stable through the night. We’ll plan to discharge you if you continue improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That would be great. I miss my routine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just checking in. Any pain or nausea since this morning?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: None at all. I even walked down the hall twice today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s fantastic. You’re clearly ready to transition home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—we’re discharging you today. You’ve had four days of monitoring, and your symptoms have significantly improved.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s wonderful. What do I need to do at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Continue tube feeds at 50 cc/hr continuously. No oral intake. Keep taking all your medications, including lansoprazole and rifaximin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about pain? I might need something if it flares up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re prescribing oxycodone 5 mg every 4 hours as needed for pain. But use it sparingly—it can cause drowsiness and constipation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I understand. I’ll stick to the ondansetron if I feel nauseous.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. And call us or go to the ER if you develop a fever over 101.5, severe pain, vomiting, or redness around your tube site.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And follow-up with surgery and GI?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your surgeon will contact you. Also, continue moderate activity—no heavy lifting, but walking is encouraged.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been doing that. I feel strong enough.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve made great progress. We’re discharging you home in stable condition. Nurse will go over your meds and feeds before you leave.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you so much. I really appreciate the care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you soon in clinic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick update—your discharge paperwork is ready. You can leave once the nurse confirms your feeds are set up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. I’ve packed everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse says you’re all set. Remember—no driving while on oxycodone.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I won’t. My husband is picking me up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. Stay hydrated, keep the feeds going, and rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing really well. We’re glad to see you improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—your ferritin and lipids are still being monitored. Keep taking your multivitamins and atorvastatin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I haven’t missed a dose. I know how important they are after bypass.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s exactly right. You’re managing your health very well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just checking—any last questions before discharge?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I think I’ve got it all. Feeds, meds, warning signs, follow-up. I’m ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll see you in the clinic soon. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Discharge is official. You’re cleared to go home now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I’m so glad to be going home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re glad too. Stay well, and call if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Have a great day.
